thread:
Anika: FYI I opened a cleanup PR to unify the quota examples across pricing, metering, and the analytics dashboard. Main goal: remove duplicate wording and add a tiny burst-credit example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/722
Theo: Link looks good. What's the burst example? short snippet?
Anika: Exactly. It's a one-paragraph explainer + a tiny dashboard panel JSON that shows 'burst_credits_used' vs 'quota_window_remaining'. The panel needs an image and a variable for datasource.
Riley: Can you paste the compact SDK snippet you plan to use? I want to sanity-check header names and the backoff note.
Anika: Added this compact JS snippet for the SDK docs card:
DocsBot: ```js
// meter headers example (compact)
await Redwood.client.generate({ model: 'redwood-xlarge', headers: { 'x-rw-meter-mode': 'billing' } })
```
Marcus: Suggestion: use 'x-rw-usage' as the canonical header. We've been inconsistent across SDK and infra. If we change it here, let's add a migration note.
Ivy: I prefer 'x-rw-meter-mode' — it's explicit. If we rename, we should include a tiny mapping table in the migration guide.
Theo: Also add a 429 handling blurb. People keep pasting naive loops. Keep it short: exponential backoff with full jitter, 3 retries, show pseudo-code.
Anika: Will do. Also the pricing table text now clarifies "per 1K tokens (prompt + completion)" and adds an embeddings example showing units billed as "per 1K vector-units".
Riley: For the dashboard panel JSON, my only ask: don't hardcode the datasource name. Use a variable like ${DS_BILLING} and document that deployments name it differently (prom_billing / billing_prom / prometheus-billing).
Anika: Done in the PR. I added a short footnote: "Datasource name varies by deployment; replace ${DS_BILLING} with your datasource."
Marcus: Metadata nit: can we add an annotation to the panel JSON so teams know which query is for billing vs which is for latency correlation? A basic description field is enough.
Anika: Good call. Added descriptions to both queries.
Ivy: I noticed a broken anchor when I ran link-check: `/usage/tiers#limits` -> the old page used `/pricing/limits`. I added a redirect entry but we should double-check other internal refs.
Theo: I grep'd the repo and found 7 other references; updated them in the PR. Also added a short migration section "If you link to pricing/limits, update to /usage/tiers#limits."
Riley: Screenshot request: can someone attach a 1200x360 banner of the panel? I can crop if needed.
Marcus: Uploaded screenshot to the PR comment (PNG, 1200x360). I also validated queries run locally with prom_billing.
Ivy: Small wording suggestion: in the burst example, change "credits are consumed" -> "credits decrement during bursts" to be clearer about timing.
Anika: Updated phrasing. Also added a tiny changelog bullet under "Docs release notes": "Unify quota examples, add burst-credit panel & small SDK header example."
Theo: I'll add the exponential backoff snippet (py pseudo) and a one-line recomendation to surface 429s as metrics in the usage dashboard.
DocsBot: Note: docs-link-check completed for PR 722 with 1 warning (anchor aliasing) — resolved in latest commits.
Riley: One remaining question: should we mention the meter aggregation window (per-minute vs per-hour) in the examples? Some customers were confused in support tickets.
Anika: Added a short note: "Billing meters are aggregated in 1m windows by default; dashboards often use 1h rollups for stability."
Marcus: LGTM from my side. If no objections, merge after CI passes and after Theo adds the backoff snippet.
Ivy: No objections. I'll watch the deploy and confirm the redirect works in prod preview.
Anika: Thanks team, merging after CI. :rocket:
